e: The Metropolitan Police launches an investigation into comedian and author David Walliams following allegations of "serious sexual offences".

Mohammed Alfatih, a former bodyguard of slain Hamas chief Ismail Haniyeh and the son of senior Hamas official Basem Naim, is found guilty of attacking a court officer who had come to collect debts from his wife outside his Birmingham home in October 2025 after being granted asylum and citizenship.
Office for National Statistics data indicates the UK economy expanded by 0.7% between July and September, its fastest growth since 2024.
Two Iranian men are convicted in the UK of spying on dissident journalists for Iranian intelligence with the intention of attacking them for their criticism of the Iranian government.
Meta have disabled social media accounts on their platforms belonging to Russell Brand.
Six more women come forward with allegations of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by Russell Brand.

A joint investigation by The Guardian and ITV News publishes allegations of sexual misconduct against comedian and children's author David Walliams, following the dismissal of his High Court bid to prevent publication. Walliams denies the allegations.
The first of a further 850 prisoners to be released early from prison to ease overcrowding walk free from prisons in England and Wales.
Russell Brand is sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assault.
It is reported that a Parole Board hearing for Jon Venables has rejected an application for parole after he told the hearing he should remain in prison.
Civil servant Kashim Chowdhury, who secretly held multiple public sector jobs on full-time salaries, is convicted of nine counts of fraud.
The United States evacuates its military aircraft from RAF Mildenhall following a reported threat from Iran.
A British citizen is reported to be among those killed in a mass shooting in Kraków, Poland.

The Bank of England raises its baseline interest rate from 3.75% to 4%, the first increase in more than three years. Andrew Bailey, the Bank's governor, says the decision "shouldn't be seen as the first in an inevitably long sequence of hikes", but warns "unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase".

Russell Brand is convicted at Southwark Crown Court of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault and remanded in custody. He will be sentenced on 9 November. Shortly after the verdict, police announce two further inquiries into allegations of rape involving Brand.
The UK's largest Harry Potter store opens in London's Oxford Street.

George Madgwick, the leader of Reform UK in Hampshire, is charged with 35 offences against four victims over a 13-year period, including rape, sexual assault, controlling or coercive behaviour, and making indecent images of a child.
A series of bomb hoaxes disrupts dozens of passenger flights across Europe, including services from Luton, Heathrow, Manchester and Stansted, as well as two easyJet flights from Britain to Prague.
Karl Bushby completes his 28-year journey around the world, without any form of transport, having covered a distance of 31,000 miles (58,000 km) which began in Chile and ended in Hull, Yorkshire.
Virgin Media O2 announces plans to cut a significant number of its workforce as it faces financial difficulties.
A demonstration in support of Palestine Action takes place outside the US embassy in London. By the following day, police have made 325 arrests in connection with the protest.
Five teenagers are seriously injured after being stabbed at a Halloween party in Chandler's Ford, Hampshire.

Simon Richardson is found guilty of murdering head teacher Michael Mullins by dragging him for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car. The judge tells Richardson he can expect life imprisonment when sentenced on Monday at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court.
Poundland files for administration, putting 12,000 jobs at risk.

Chancellor John Healey delivers the 2026 United Kingdom budget, the first under Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Key measures include a £100 energy payment for 20 million households, the abolition of standing charges on gas bills, an extension of the temporary VAT cut on electricity, and a 3.9% increase in the minimum and living wages from April 2027. A temporary rise in the bank corporation tax surcharge from 3% to 6% is announced to fund energy support, while the £20,000 annual cash ISA allowance is retained. The Office for Budget Responsibility forecasts economic growth of 1.2% in 2026 and 1% in 2027.
King Charles arrives in the Bahamas to begin nine day tour of the Caribbean, his first as monarch.
Two British nationals appear at Westminster Magistrates Court in connection with an alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford, and are remanded in custody to appear at the Old Bailey in November.
Oxford Street in central London, the UK's most famous shopping street, is pedestrianised between the junctions of Orchard Street and Great Portland Street.

Storm Boelo: Two men are reported to have been killed by falling trees, while the number of properties without power increases to 90,000. The Met Office issues a new yellow warning for strong winds from 18:00 on Monday 26 October to 03:00 on Tuesday 27 October across the west coast of England, Wales and Scotland and eastern parts of Northern Ireland.
An independent inquiry is announced into the circumstances surrounding the murder of Henry Nowak.
US singer Chris Brown is given an eight month prison sentence suspended for 12 months for striking a man with a tequila bottle in a London nightclub.
Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or, becoming the first English footballer to win the prize in 25 years.

Storm Boelo: The storm brings winds of up to 84 mph, widespread flooding and major transport disruption to Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England, leaving more than 82,000 properties without electricity.
The Board of Deputies of British Jews declares the Green Party to be a racist party following its backing of a motion that Zionism is racist.
Storm Boelo: Amber weather alerts for high winds and heavy rain come into force for northern parts of the UK.

Storm Austen: More than 13,000 homes in Wales, Cornwall, Devon and other parts of England are affected by power cuts caused by Storm Austen. A yellow weather warning for wind is in place across England and Wales.

Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets take part in a French nuclear deterrent exercise over the Mediterranean Sea amid increased regional security concerns brought on by Russia's ongoing invasion of Ukraine. Codenamed "Exercise Rummy," it is the first time that France and the UK have collaborated to simulate an airborne nuclear attack.

Authorities in the Philippines confirm an investigation into allegations that Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, possessed child sexual abuse images. Markle denies the allegations, while the Duchess says she is "deeply distressed" and reveals that she was informed of earlier allegations against her father in 2018.

Following the discovery of a high-impact security vulnerability in PHP, a programming language used by most of the World Wide Web, many websites are temporarily taken offline as a precautionary measure. The UK government says it is working to identify any potential exposure of its online services, and urges "all organisations, private and public, large and small" to follow guidance to protect their systems.
In cricket, captain Harry Brook becomes the first England batter to make a double century in a one-day international, with 202 runs against Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi.
